events.description: Abu Muhammad al-Masri killed in Tehran with his daughter Miriam (widow of Hamza bin Laden) in an Israeli operation at the behest of the CIA (host misspoke the year as 1998)
Rumors that Zawahiri died of ill health; UN Monitoring Team found zero confirmation and assumes he is alive
Last radio broadcast by ISIS spokesman Abu Hamza al-Qurashi (fourth during al-Mawla's tenure), described as frustrated and uninspiring
Al-Mawla (Haji Abdullah) took over the Islamic State after Baghdadi's death; 'just over a year' / 'a year and a quarter' before Feb 2021
actors: Amir Muhammad Said Abd al-Rahman al-Mawla

events.description: Secretary of State Pompeo's speech highlighting al-Qaeda general manager al-Maghrebi's presence in Iran; too late and not member-state confirmed for the UN report
AQIS emir Asim Umar killed in a Taliban stronghold in Helmand
Taliban secured the release of Asim Umar's wife (believed Pakistani) from Afghan custody as part of prisoner releases
US-Taliban Doha agreement; US out, NATO forces likely out by May 2021; Taliban 11 months later still says al-Qaeda does not exist in Afghanistan
Deadline under the Doha agreement for US withdrawal; Biden must decide whether to keep 2,500 troops
Haqqani Network in talks with al-Qaeda leadership about standing up a new fighting force in Afghanistan, which some sources call the first army of the resurrected Islamic Emirate
TTP statement proclaiming complete reunification as Jamaat-ul-Ahrar and the Mehsud group of South Waziristan rejoined; UN credits al-Qaeda with bringing them back together
AQAP emir Khalid Batarfi reportedly arrested late 2020 in an operation that also killed a significant figure (UN member-state briefings)
AQAP lost its previous emir Qasim al-Raymi early in 2020 and its master bomb maker
AQIM emir Abdelmalek Droukdel killed; believed fifth in al-Qaeda's succession line
ISCAP captured and continues to hold the port of Mocimboa da Praia despite a sustained government offensive (date per UN report; approx)
ISCAP cross-border operations into southern Tanzania during the UN reporting period
Major ISCAP jailbreak in the DRC releasing huge numbers of prisoners
Release of the UN Monitoring Team's latest ISIL/al-Qaeda report discussed in this episode; previous reports around end of May 2020 (Afghanistan) and July 2020

key_claims: Al-Mawla is firmly in charge of ISIS but publicly silent, relying on spokesman Abu Hamza; silence risks ISIS looking like 'yesterday's news'.
Zawahiri is elderly and in poor health; October 2020 death rumors are unconfirmed and the UN assumes he is alive; al-Qaeda must plan succession.
Abu Muhammad al-Masri, Zawahiri's number two, was killed in Tehran on 7 Aug 2020 with his daughter (Hamza bin Laden's widow); Saif al-Adel in Iran is now the most likely successor.
Al-Qaeda's 'core' vs 'affiliate' distinction is blurred: succession can pass to leaders in regional branches (e.g. Droukdel was number five) and the top leadership could even end up in Africa.
Abd al-Rahman al-Maghrebi, Moroccan son-in-law of Zawahiri, is al-Qaeda's general manager overseeing communications with branches and is reportedly in Iran.
UN finds no significant change in Taliban-al-Qaeda relations; the Taliban keeps publicly denying al-Qaeda's presence while freeing the wife of slain AQIS emir Asim Umar.
The Haqqani Network, integral to the Taliban, incubated al-Qaeda and is in talks with al-Qaeda about a new fighting force; UN also sees Haqqani involvement in ISKP.
The TTP has reunified (Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Mehsud faction) under Noor Wali Mehsud with al-Qaeda's mediation; ~6,000 fighters and several hundred cross-border attacks.
AQAP has been badly weakened: al-Raymi killed, Batarfi reportedly arrested, violent conflict with ISIS and the Houthis.
ISCAP is growing stronger, holding the port of Mocimboa da Praia and operating into Tanzania, with Somalia as the regional hub.
